title: MSI-VISUAL: New visualization methods for Mass Spectrometry Imaging and tools for interactive mapping and exploration of m/z values
projectDescription: Mass spectrometry imaging dataset from fresh frozen mouse brain sections for development of a novel spatial segmentation computational pipeline.
sampleProcessingProtocol:
The new mouse brain dataset (PXD056609, internal number: NRL4485-s2) was generated using frozen hemispheres of four 100-day-old animals in the C57Bl/6J background (internal number: 32156, 36197, 46711, 47823). Two mice (32156, 46711) expressed combined human mutated APP and a PS1-mutated transgenes (APPtg) for the generation of beta-amyloid plaques [1]. Frozen mouse hemispheres were coronary cut in 10µm thick sections using a cryomicrotome (CM1950, Leica, Nussloch, Germany) and placed on a single Intellislide® (Bruker, Bremen, Germany). The section was dried in a vacuum chamber and sprayed with N-(1-Naphthyl) ethylenediamine dihydrochloride (NEDC) matrix dissolved to 7mg/ml in 70% methanol using a HTX3+ TM Sprayer (HTX technologies, Carrboro, NC, USA) as described by Andersen et al. [2]. Matrix-assisted laser desorption ionization trapped ion mobility mass spectrometry imaging (MALDI-TIMS-MSI) was performed in negative mode using a timsTOF fleX™ mass spectrometer (Bruker Corporation, Bremen, Germany). Mass calibration was performed using red phosphorous and ion mobility using ESI-L Low Concentration Tuning Mix (Agilent Technologies, Santa Clara, CA, USA) in ESI mode. For MALDI-TIMS-MSI analysis, a mass range of m/z 300 – 1350 and a range of the inverse reduced mobility (1/K0) of 0.7–1.8 Vs/cm2 was used. The laser was operated at a frequency of 10 kHz with a burst of 200 shots per pixel with a spatial resolution of 20µm. All four mouse hemispheres were assessed in a single overnight run.

1.	Radde, R. et al. Abeta42-driven cerebral amyloidosis in transgenic mice reveals early and robust pathology. EMBO Rep 7, 940-946 (2006).
2.	Andersen, M.K. et al. Spatial differentiation of metabolism in prostate cancer tissue by MALDI-TOF MSI. Cancer Metab 9, 9 (2021).
